key_insight: A neural-network-based inverse design framework can efficiently recover the modal coefficients needed to synthesize desired cascaded-mode near-field landscapes in multimode waveguides.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable, remote shaping of optical near-fields for applications such as microscopy and nanoparticle manipulation without relying solely on local nanostructure fabrication.
method: Train multilayer neural networks to map design parameters to near-field landscapes.
Use the trained models in a gradient-based optimization loop to reconstruct target field profiles.
Improve lateral-field design by selecting and augmenting training data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful reconstruction of both simple and complex longitudinal landscapes, with lateral-field performance improving after data-selection and augmentation strategies.
watch_item: Lateral field reconstruction remains more difficult than longitudinal design, so performance may depend strongly on training data quality and coverage.
paper_title: Neural Networks for Inverse Design of Cascaded-Mode Near-Field Landscapes
